summary: Jaroslav Průšek was a sinologist who studied at Charles University (Faculty of Arts) around 1924–1930 and later taught Karel Werner.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied at the University of Sydney (BA Honours, 2005) and the University of Oxford (DPhil, 2013) under Alexis Sanderson and Peter Oldmeadow. He held posts at Oxford, SOAS, and the University of Alberta.
Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Kosho Itagaki. He became a professor of philosophy at Seattle University around 2007.

Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Michigan (BS) and the University of California, Los Angeles (PhD, 2014) under Gregory Schopen. He served as a lecturer at UCLA.

Jason Neelis is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Texas at Austin and the University of Washington (PhD, 2001) under Richard G. Salomon. He held posts at Washington, Florida, Ruhr University Bochum, and Wilfrid Laurier University.

Jason Protass works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick and held posts as a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica and a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University.

Jay Holt Valentine is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delaware, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia (PhD), where he was supervised by Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

Jay Jasanoff is an Indo-European linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (BA ca. 1959–1963). He held faculty posts at UC Berkeley (ca. 1968–1971), Harvard (1970–1978; from 1998 as Diebold Professor), and Cornell University (1981–1985).

Jay L. Garfield is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hampshire College, Smith College, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, the University of Melbourne, and the National University of Singapore.
Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar and served as Reader of Sanskrit at Gujarat University.

Jayandra Soni is an Indologist and philosopher. He completed PhDs at Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University, and held academic posts at BHU, McMaster, the University of Marburg (1991–2012), and the University of Innsbruck.
Jayashree D. Sathe is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who served as editor in chief and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Jaś Elsner is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at King's College, Cambridge, Harvard, and the Courtauld Institute. His main posts include the Courtauld Institute, Corpus Christi College, Oxford, and the University of Oxford.
Jean Dantinne was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte and served as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian. He taught at Suryavarman II School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras, and held research and associate appointments at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He directed the French Institute of Pondicherry (1955–1977) and the EFEO (1956–1977), and held chairs at EPHE (1941–1978) and Collège de France (1951–1978).

Jean Kellens is an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguist who studied at the universities of Liège and Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held posts at the University of Liège, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, and the Collège de France.
Jean Petitot is a philosopher and linguist who studied at the École Polytechnique (1964–1966) and later served as its director around 2000–2006.

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Amsterdam. He worked with the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and served as director at Leiden University and the Kern Institute.

Jean Przyluski was an Indologist and linguist who studied at EPHE and the École Nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer. He held professorships at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France.
